title: Bivariant Hodge Atoms I: Hecke Collisions and Mixed-Hodge Coefficient Extensions
content: We investigate whether the specialization and extension structures of singular Hodge atoms can be organized compatibly with Hecke correspondences and their composition, as a step toward potential connections with geometric Langlands. Inspired by Gaitsgory’s nearby-cycle approach to affine-Hecke convolution, we develop explicit mixed-Hodge-module comparisons for GL2 and GL3 Hecke collisions, using finite-dimensional incidence geometry and Grothendieck–Springer resolutions. Our principal result reveals that derived composition and coefficient-level extensions retain fundamentally different information: in a transverse compound-A2 collision, the composition-defect triangle splits while all three underlying coefficient extensions remain nonsplit. A complementary GL2 calculation shows that isomorphic nearby cycles and trivial unipotent monodromy can conceal distinct specialization morphisms and nontrivial extensions. These results establish concrete, morphism-sensitive models for studying singular Hodge-theoretic information under geometric composition. They motivate a systematic progression toward higher-rank Hecke geometry, global Springer-orbit gluing, and prospective Hecke–Hitchin and geometric-Langlands realizations.
